title.value: Layerwise Early Stopping for Test Time Adaptation
title.justification: The title is explicitly stated multiple times throughout the paper including the first page and matches the theme of the research which focuses on a new method for test time adaptation called LEAST.
title.quote: Layerwise Early Stopping for Test Time Adaptation

analysis.description: The paper introduces Layerwise Early Stopping (LEAST), a novel approach to Test Time Adaptation (TTA) which aims to address distribution shifts by dynamically stopping adaptation in individual layers of a pretrained model when the features being learned do not contribute positively to the new domain. The technique employs a gradient-based metric to inform stopping decisions without requiring supervised labels, thereby balancing adaptation and retention of previously learned features. Extensive experiments reveal LEAST's superior performance and efficiency across multiple datasets, domain shifts, model architectures, and loss functions.

type.justification: The paper includes extensive experiments to demonstrate the effectiveness of the LEAST method, indicating an empirical approach.
type.quote: Through extensive experiments, we demonstrate that Layerwise Early Stopping improves the performance of existing TTA approaches across multiple datasets, domain shifts, model architectures, and TTA losses.

name.justification: The research primarily focuses on improving Test Time Adaptation methods, as explicitly mentioned in the abstract and throughout the paper.
name.quote: Test Time Adaptation (TTA) addresses the problem of distribution shift by enabling pretrained models to learn new features on an unseen domain at test time.

name.justification: The paper discusses a parameter-efficient adaptation method through layerwise early stopping.
name.quote: Keywords: test time adaptation · parameter efficient adaptation

name.justification: The paper is concerned with adapting models to new domains effectively, which is a typical goal of domain generalization strategies.
name.quote: LEAST outperforms standard ERM (no adaptation), all layers baselines, and other layer selection baselines (i.e., AutoRGN and AutoSNR [15]) for TTA.

name.justification: The ResNet-18 model is used in the experiments to assess LEAST's performance.
name.quote: We consider two backbones: ResNet-18 and ResNet-50, with batch normalization layers and two adaptation losses: pseudo-labeling (PL) [14] and SHOT [18].
